Turkish · Breakfast

Menemen

Turkish scrambled eggs cooked slowly into a base of peppers and tomatoes until just set — soft, saucy and eaten straight from the pan with bread.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(1,466)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 1466 reviews 25 min total Serves 2 servings Easy Turkish
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

The eggs go in over very low heat and are stirred slowly so their proteins set into soft, loose curds suspended in the tomato rather than firming into dry lumps. Cooking the peppers down for a full ten minutes first drives off water so the finished dish is saucy, not watery.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Heat the olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium heat and cook the chopped peppers for 8 to 10 minutes until completely soft and beginning to colour.

  2. Add the tomatoes, pul biber, oregano and half the salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes have collapsed into a thick sauce and the oil separates at the edges.

  3. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting.

  4. Crack the eggs directly into the pan and season with the remaining salt and the black pepper.

  5. Stir slowly with a wooden spoon, folding the eggs through the tomato, for 3 to 4 minutes. Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly underdone and glossy.

  6. The residual heat will finish them. Menemen should be soft and saucy, never dry.

  7. Scatter with the crumbled cheese and parsley and serve immediately in the pan, with bread for scooping.

Chef’s Tips

  • Low and slow with the eggs. Menemen is not a fast scramble.
  • Whether the eggs are stirred through or left whole is a regional argument in Turkey; both are correct.
  • Peel the tomatoes if you have the time — the skins curl into unpleasant strips otherwise.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Turkish tea, served in a tulip glass
  • Serve with olives, cucumber, white cheese and bread
  • Follow with fresh fruit

Storage & Reheating

Best immediately. The pepper and tomato base keeps 3 days refrigerated — reheat and add fresh eggs.
